as_told.title: Corso had 24 hours to edit The Day After Roswell

plain: The story is that the 1997 book The Day After Roswell, written by Philip J. Corso with William J. Birnes, was rushed to print. The book is about Roswell, New Mexico, where something is said to have crashed in 1947, and Corso claims in it to have handled what was recovered. A UFO investigator named James Fox says Corso himself told how the book was hurried out with Birnes, and Fox also names a man called Michael Hessman. An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb (UAP stands for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the newer word for UFOs) adds a rumour that Corso had only 24 hours to edit it. UAPGerb also passes on Corso's son's account: that Corso put his hand to his head and said, "I can't believe this." Both are repeating what others told them, not what they saw. The point of the story is that if the book was rushed, its mistakes might come from haste rather than from Corso making things up.
